added_claims.quote: Economics is not really a hard science.
added_claims.claim: Because human responses to policy are emotional and unpredictable, economics and investing cannot be tested like chemistry or biology; mechanical models of flows must be treated as only half the answer and controlled-experiment confidence is unavailable.

added_claims.claim: There is no agreed definition of money (Austrians say gold, Keynesians a monetary aggregate such as M2, and economists switch among MZM, M1, M2, M3), so money-supply arguments depend heavily on which measure is chosen.

added_claims.speaker: Cullen Roche
added_claims.quote: the Fed lets the long end float and banks will try to front run and change long term rates because they know that the monopolist isn’t actually setting that rate
added_claims.claim: Long yields float around expectations of where the Fed will take the short rate (dog on a leash); if the Fed announced a target such as 10-year at 3% it would be reached within days since no one can arbitrage the reserve monopolist, but yield curve control would sacrifice the market signal the free long end provides.
added_claims.indicator: long-term yields vs policy rate path
